title: Gigs (content/rules/gigs.json, schema v0)
description: The side jobs of the game as data: the numbers of the board of a city (how often it changes, how many offers it has in each phase of the day, how rare the good ones are), what a gig pays and how long it may be at each level of the driver, and the templates that the offers are drawn from. A gig is a round trip of a car with passengers or a load: the car leaves its track for the time it takes, and is paid when it is back. Provisional, like the rules.

enabled.description: Whether the game has gigs. Off means no board and no new gigs; a gig that is on the road is finished.

unlock_after_step.description: The step of the tutorial after which the board opens (a driver who left the tutorial has it at once).

timezone.description: The time zone in which the day of the daily limit starts.

reset_hour.description: The hour (in that time zone) at which the day of the daily limit starts.

wave_ms.description: How long the offers of a city stay the same: the board is made again, from the seed, once a wave. 1 350 000 is the 22,5 minutes of a piece of weather.

cancel_window_ms.description: How long after taking a gig the driver may take it back, with the fuel returned and nothing lost but the laps of those seconds.

slots.description: How many offers a city has in a wave that begins in each phase of the day.

rarities.description: How good an offer is: its weight in the draw (a weight of 5 against 70 is about one in fifteen) and what it multiplies the pay by. The first is the ordinary one.

ref_speed_kmh.description: The speed at which the time of a gig is counted for its pay (the reference time): a gig of 70 km pays for an hour at 70.

speed_cap_kmh.description: The fastest a car drives on a gig (the roads have limits), so that a fast car finishes sooner but not without end.

xp_per_hour.description: The experience of the driver for an hour of the reference time of a gig.

car_xp_per_hour.description: The experience of the car for an hour of the reference time of a gig.

anchors.description: What an hour of driving pays after the fuel at the rung of the ladder of cars that a level opens, in cents (the anchors of the economy: 600 * 1.15 ^ rung dollars). A gig pays by the rung of the car that does it, which is the one its own level opens.

bands.description: What the level of the driver changes: the part of the anchor that a gig pays, the longest gig (in minutes of the reference time) the board offers, and how many gigs a driver may take in a day. They rise with the level because the window in which a car drives on one tank grows, and a gig is worth less against it.

kinds.description: The kinds of gig, with their names in the languages of the game.

templates.description: What the offers are drawn from. Each has a kind, what it asks of the car (a number of seats or a load, and maybe a class), how long a trip may be, and how likely it is in each phase of the day.

capacity.description: What the car is asked for: `seats` for people, `cargo_kg` for a load.

amount.description: How many people or how many kilograms an offer carries.

class_in.description: If set, only a car of one of these classes can take the gig (the delivery vehicles).

mode.description: `local` is a trip in the city (its length is in `local_km`); `intercity` is to another city that the driver's level has opened, and back.

local_km.description: For a local gig: the length of the whole trip, in km.

pay_ppm.description: What this template multiplies the pay by (1 000 000 is the plain pay).

phase_pay_ppm.description: A multiplier of the pay for the phase of the day the offer appeared in (dusk fever for taxis, the night rate). A phase that is not here pays plain.

phases.description: The weight of the template in the draw of an offer that appears in each phase of the day (0 is never).

window_waves.description: How many waves an offer of this template stays on the board.

deadline_ppm.description: If set, the car must finish within this part of the reference time (1 000 000 is exactly the time at the reference speed): a slow car cannot take an express.

night.description: The night run: one opportunity for each game night in each city, a small load across the border of the law that pays several times the plain pay and may be stopped by the police. The driver sees the chances before they take it. It is not one of the templates because it is not drawn from the board: it is made once for a night, from the seed.

enabled.description: Whether the night run is offered. Off means no opportunity; a night run that is on the road is finished.

kind.description: The kind of the offer, one of the kinds of the document.

amount.description: How many kilograms the load is.

pay_ppm.description: What the night run multiplies the plain pay of the same trip by (2 500 000 is two and a half times).

daily_limit.description: How many night runs a driver may take in a day (the day of the daily limit of the gigs).

control_ppm.description: The chance that the patrols stop a night run, before the car changes it.

modifiers.description: What the body class of the car changes in that chance: a quiet car draws less attention, a loud one more.

escape_ppm.description: Of the stops, the part that the car drives away from; the rest is an arrest.

heat_ms.description: How long after an escape the patrols of that city look harder for the car.

heat_ppm.description: How much more the chance of a stop is in that time.

escape_pay_ppm.description: The part of the pay that a car which got away is paid.

ms.description: How long the arrest lasts from the moment of the stop. It blocks the journeys and the gigs of the driver, and nothing else.

fine_ppm.description: The fine, as a part of the pay of the night run, taken when the car is back (never more than the driver has).

bail_ppm.description: The bail, as a part of the same pay: what the driver pays to end the arrest at once.
